discovery: Discovery of the Fermi bubbles: giant gamma-ray lobes extending from the Galactic Center

nominees.name: Douglas P. Finkbeiner
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University / Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian

subfield: High-energy astrophysics / Galactic outflows and cosmic rays
motivation: In 2010 Su, Slatyer and Finkbeiner found two enormous gamma-ray lobes, each extending about 50 degrees (roughly 8 kpc) above and below the Galactic Center, in public Fermi-LAT data. They did it with careful template subtraction of foreground emission. The bubbles have hard spectra, sharp edges and match the WMAP microwave haze and ROSAT X-ray features. Together these show that our own Galaxy has had a powerful energetic outflow within the last few million years, driven by either the central black hole or a nuclear starburst. The discovery made Galactic feedback measurable. It gave a nearby laboratory, with resolved structure, for cosmic-ray acceleration and transport, for shocks and for the energy budget of galactic winds. It led to follow-up in radio polarization, UV absorption spectroscopy and X-rays, culminating in the eROSITA bubbles. It changed how we think about the Milky Way's nucleus and how galaxies regulate themselves.
